l: 1. Portable radios shall be issued to all sworn personnel and some non-sworn employees based on work assignment or operational needs.

a. Due to the specific configurations for department radios, all radios shall be assigned through City Radio Services. Radios shall not be purchased from any other source and service will only be provided to department radios.

2. When in uniform, personnel issued a portable radio are required to carry them at all times. While away from their primary duty station or mobile radio, all employees will have their portable radios on and able to receive communications.
3. Reserve officers and civilian employees who are issued portable radios shall use them only while on duty and the radios shall be secured by the employee while off-duty.
a. Any exceptions for civilian employees and reserve officers for off-duty usage shall require written approval by the Chief of Police or designee.
4. Officers transferring from one unit to another unit shall retain the portable radio and related equipment which they have been issued.

a. Officers transferring from a division shall take their portable radio to the City Radio Services for reprogramming. Only officers transferred via a Personnel Order shall be eligible for portable radio reprogramming. Officers who need portable radio reprogramming for other reasons must obtain a signed inter-office correspondence from the deputy chief and take this form and their portable radio to the City Radio Services.

5. Changes in the issuance of portable radios and accessories will be forwarded to the Finance and Personnel Bureau from City Radio Services. All commissioned officers will be issued portable radios if they are available.
6. In the event an employee is assigned to a division and no portable radios are available, the division captain shall direct a written request to the City Radio Services for a portable radio.
7. City Radio Services shall maintain a pool of radios for use in the event of equipment malfunction and for special operations, or other similar circumstances.
B. Police Asset Management and City Radio Services shall be responsible for the inventory of portable radio equipment which has been assigned to officers and divisions throughout the department.
C. Use of Portable Radios While Off-Duty
1. Portable radios shall be used off-duty only during exigent circumstances, i.e., where the reporting of an incident will reduce the threat of imminent or possible harm to life or property.

2. The use of portable radios while off-duty for unit-to-unit or unit-to-base station (other than Police Communications Division) contact is prohibited, except following the report of an incident where further communications can provide an additional safety factor for responding officers.
3. The use of portable radios while off-duty to request information from the Police Information Center or any other unit is prohibited.
4. When using a portable radio while off-duty, proper radio discipline shall be followed as outlined in General Order 604.01, Radio Discipline.
a. Employees using a portable radio off-duty shall use the alpha prefix “R” and then their identification number when contacting the dispatcher while off-duty.

5. The mere reporting of an eligible incident via a portable radio while off-duty shall not warrant any compensation, either monetary or compensatory time, and shall not place the employee in an on-duty status.
6. When engaged in off-duty law enforcement and security-related (LE/SR) employment, use of the portable radio shall be in compliance with the provisions for off-duty use of portable radios.
7. Any exceptions to provisions for off-duty LE/SR employment use of portable radios shall require written approval by the Chief of Police or designee.
D. Responsibility for Issued Portable Radios

1. Any employee assigned a portable radio is responsible for the proper care and maintenance of the equipment. All personnel shall use due diligence to ensure that no issued item of equipment is damaged, lost, or stolen.
2. In the event a portable radio is damaged or becomes non-functional, it shall be swapped out in a one for one exchange with the City Radio Services.
a. A supervisor receiving a damaged or malfunctioning radio shall follow division guidelines for obtaining the repair of the equipment.

b. If the supervisor suspects the radio was damaged due to negligence, they shall conduct an investigation and provide a written report to the captain of their division reporting their findings. A copy of the report shall be sent to the City Radio Services.
c. During the time an officer’s assigned radio is being repaired, the officer shall check out a pool radio from the City Radio Services.

3. The loss or theft of any portable radio shall be reported to a supervisor within the affected employee’s division immediately and the supervisor shall ensure that the City Radio Services is notified.

a. Within seventy-two (72) hours after the discovery of the loss or theft of an assigned portable radio, following the above notification, the employee shall submit a written report of the circumstances of the loss or theft of the radio to their supervisor. The supervisor shall submit the report to the division captain through the appropriate chain of command.

b. In the event of the theft of the portable radio, it shall be reported to the appropriate police jurisdiction immediately and an offense report shall be completed. The employee shall ensure that the agency is provided with the manufacturer’s name, model number, and serial number of the radio in order to allow entry into the NCIC system. If the employee does not have the serial number, they shall obtain it from the City Radio Services at the earliest possible time and provide it to the agency who took the offense report.

c. The division captain shall ensure that an investigation is completed regarding the loss or theft of the radio and that the completed report of the investigation is forwarded to the appropriate deputy chief with a copy being sent to the City Radio Services. When a radio is damaged, lost or stolen due to negligence, as determine by an investigation of the circumstances, the disciplinary process shall be followed to address the misconduct.

E. Portable radios may be temporarily assigned to other law enforcement agencies, if available, or personnel upon written request from the agency or individual involved and after written approval of the Chief of Police has been obtained.
1. The Police Communications Division shall have primary responsibility for reporting violations of this order regarding the misuse of portable radios while off-duty.
a. The dispatcher detecting the violation shall contact their supervisor and inform them of the nature of the violation, the time it occurred, and the radio call number of the violator.
b. The supervisor shall complete an Inter-Office Correspondence containing the above information and forward it to their Assistant Chief through the chain of command.
c. The Assistant Chief shall forward the report of misuse to the deputy chief of the person allegedly committing the violation.
d. It shall be the responsibility of the deputy chief of the employee allegedly committing the infraction to investigate the complaint and take appropriate disciplinary action.

2. Although the Police Communications Division has primary responsibility for reporting infractions, this does not relieve field supervisors from the responsibility of noting and reporting violations of this General Order.

A. Employees who are issued departmental electronic devices, including cellular phones with messaging functions, shall have the device with them at all times and will monitor the device for incoming messages and calls. Employees shall answer all calls or messages in a timely manner unless the employee is aware the telephone number is one that has been used for telephone harassment.
1. As per General Order 406.08, Call-Back Pay, off-duty employees using an electronic device shall not report work time if the employee is able to use their time effectively for their own purposes.

a. Employees on scheduled vacation, holidays, Workers Comp Control Group or Extended Leave Control Group, or sick or occupational leave shall not be responsible for monitoring their devices, unless exigent circumstances exist and prior approval has been received by their supervisor.

B. Personnel authorized to use departmental electronic devices, including cellular telephones, shall use the devices in a professional manner, consistent with the rules for radio discipline covered in General Order 604.01, Radio Discipline.
C. Employees shall limit the use of departmental cellular telephones for personal or non-departmental matters. Personal or non-departmental long distance calls are prohibited.

1. Employees shall be responsible for reimbursement to the department for all charges for long distance, roamer, and directory assistance related to personal calls both outgoing and incoming at 100% of the charges.
2. Employees shall limit long distance, roamer, or directory assistance calls for departmental business to emergency situations only.

D. Any abuse in the use of electronic devices which indicates an inordinate amount of time is being used for either incoming or outgoing personal calls or messages will be considered as neglect of duty and disciplinary action may be taken.

E. All personnel should be aware that a cellular phone is not a secure phone and that conversations can be intercepted and monitored by skilled personnel using easily available radio scanners. Sensitive conversations should always be conducted on a secure land line.
F. All electronic devices, including cellular phones, equipped with a locking code will be locked when the device is unattended.

G. While attending meetings, training, public events, or other situations were an audible mode could be disruptive, the device shall be set on a silent mode, if the device is equipped with that function.

H. Any employee authorized to use departmental electronic devices, including cellular telephones, will be responsible for the proper care of the equipment and shall use due diligence to ensure the device is not damaged, lost, or stolen.

1. Any employee whose departmentally-owned electronic device, including a cellular phone, is lost, stolen, or misplaced shall immediately notify their supervisor and an incident or offense report shall be generated.

I. No employee may use a personal electronic device, including a cell phone, to photograph or electronically record any crime scene or potential criminal evidence without prior approval of their supervisor. In accordance with General Order 224.04, Social Media, employees shall not post department photos to social media. As outlined in General Order 212.09, Photographs/Recordings of Deceased Persons at Crime Scenes or Non-Criminal Deaths, any unauthorized release or sharing of the photograph, recording, or other record of a crime scene or of a deceased person is strictly prohibited.

J. Employees are prohibited from taking or transmitting digital images, including videos, in any location that a person would have a reasonable expectation of privacy, including but not limited to, meetings, locker rooms, classrooms, or testing areas. without the subject's knowledge and permission. Violations of this order may result in the equipment being confiscated as evidence and the employee subject to disciplinary action.

K. Employees may carry personally-owned electronic devices, including cellular phones, instead of the department-issued device on-duty only after receiving written permission from a supervisor. When used on-duty, if City business is conducted on a personally-owned electronic devices and the City has a warrant or consent, it may be subject to Public Information Requests.
1. Employees electing to carry a personally-owned device instead of a departmental device shall be held to the same standard outlined in this General Order.

2. When electing to carry a personal device rather than a departmental device, the employee shall immediately provide the phone number to Employment Services Section and promptly report any changes to the device's number.
3. Personally-owned electronic devices, including cell phones and smart phones, are not eligible for replacement per General Order 509.02, Replacement of Equipment.
L. Proper cellular phone and other electronic device etiquette should be followed by all employees when dealing with the public.

1. Use discretion with the use of electronic devices in public places. Unless it is an emergency, never talk on the cell phone in elevators, libraries, auditoriums, classrooms, meetings or other enclosed public spaces. Silence or turn off your phone in areas such as doctor offices or hospital emergency rooms.

2. Unless it involves the service call, do not talk on a cellular phone or text while in direct contact with the public. When in face to face contact with the public, do not wear cellular phone accessories such as ear buds or bluetooth headsets.

The Fort Worth Police Department is committed to establishing a Body-Worn Camera program that reinforces its responsibility for protecting the public, for officer safety and enhancing professionalism through transparency and accountability to effectively document law enforcement contacts, while taking into account legitimate individual privacy interests.
A. Body-Worn Camera Policy not applicable to other recording systems; personal recording devices prohibited.

1. The guidelines in this order apply only to body-worn cameras that attach directly to a uniform or person. These guidelines do not apply to the use of the in-car fixed audio/video recording systems mounted in Fort Worth Police Department vehicles. The guidelines for in-car video are outlined in General Order 506.04, In-Car Recording System.

2. Department Employees are prohibited from utilizing personally-owned digital recording devices while on-duty or while engaged in approved off-duty law enforcement and security-related (LE/SR) employment; however, employees shall utilize a city-owned Body Worn Camera (BWC) pursuant to this General Order and applicable statutory laws cited herein. TBP 1.11
B. Distribution, training, and maintenance of Body-Worn Cameras (BWC)
1. All sworn officers and Civilian Response personnel, regardless of rank or assignment, may be issued a BWC.

2. Any employee issued a BWC shall attend department-approved training on the device, review the standard operating procedures governing its use and demonstrate a working knowledge of the device prior to employing it in field operations or off-duty LE/SR.
3. Supervisors of employees issued a BWC shall attend department-approved training regarding the device as well as the procedures for storing and retention of digital media evidence (DME).

4. In the event that a BWC is lost, the employee shall immediately notify their supervisor and submit a police report for lost property. The supervisor shall ensure the employee completes an Equipment Replacement Request on the date of the loss, or as soon as possible in cases involving employee injury, and submit/route the approved request through the chain of command to the Body Camera Program Coordinator for appropriate action.
5. Department employees may be subject to disciplinary action for reporting to duty without their assigned BWC and/or for the intentional, negligent loss of, or damage to, a device.
The Body Worn-Camera shall be affixed to the employee’s shirt or uniform in a location and manner that maximizes the camera’s ability to capture video footage of the employee’s activities.
D. Rules for use of Body-Worn Cameras

The rules for use of body worn cameras described in this subsection apply to all Civilian Response personnel, members of the Abandoned Vehicle Enforcement Unit and uniformed officers, regardless of rank (collectively, “Investigating Employee”). For the purpose of this subsection, “investigation” means the gathering or collecting of facts, information, or evidence, including statements, which may be used to determine whether a crime has occurred or may occur. Pursuant to Texas Occupations Code 1701.657, Investigating Employees equipped with a BWC must act in a manner that is consistent with this policy with respect to when and under what circumstances a body worn camera must be activated.
1. Activation and deactivation of BWC by Investigating Employees

a. For purposes of this order, deactivation of the BWC means the use of the “sleep mode”. “Sleep mode” may be utilized for situations were officers are allowed by policy to temporarily deactivate the BWC for privacy-related situations (i.e. restroom breaks, meal breaks, private conversations, etc.).

(1) “Sleep mode” is not an option while officers are conducting an active investigation. The “mute” function should be utilized during these instances if tactics, training issues, or CJIS-protected conversations are taking place.
(2) Powering off the BWC is strongly discouraged and should only be used at the end of shift or when charging the BWC.
b. The BWC, including all audio functions, shall be activated under the following circumstances:
(1) Collection of evidence that can be used in the prosecution of criminal offenses, except for collection of evidence by the Crime Scene Search Unit;
(2) Pursuits by vehicle and on foot;
(4) Investigations of calls involving mentally-distressed persons;
(5) Documentation of accident or crime scenes, etc.;

(6) Dynamic and deliberate tactical entry operations, unless precluded by an existing Memorandum Of Understanding (MOU), law enforcement task force agreement, or any other agreement with a federal agency;
(7) Contacts with members of the public when law enforcement action will potentially be taken or is being taken;
(8) Encounters with any person in connection with an investigation;

(9) To record any on-scene interviews conducted by a detective. A detective shall not conduct an on-scene interview of a victim, witness, or suspect unless accompanied by a uniformed officer who shall activate the BWC to capture the entirety of the on-scene encounter between a detective and victim, witness, or suspect; and

c. Pursuant to Texas Occupations Code 1701.655 and 1701.657, Investigating Employees equipped with a body worn camera and actively participating in an investigation shall keep the camera activated for the entirety of the Investigating Employee's active participation in the investigation unless the camera has been deactivated in compliance with this policy. For purposes of this section, officers not actively participating in the investigation, such as an officer standing on a perimeter and not taking any police action, may place their BWC in sleep mode during that time period.

d. The BWC may also be temporarily deactivated under the following circumstances, provided that the employee who deactivates the BWC verbally states why the employee is choosing to deactivate the BWC prior to doing so and the BWC is immediately reactivated once the basis for deactivation is over:
(1) Facilitating discussions of training issues or operation strategies that involve officer-safety issues;
(2) Sharing telephone numbers, home addresses, or social security numbers of police department employees or police department employees’ family members;
(3) Conducting conversations containing privileged information (i.e. communication with Clergy, Police Peer Counselors, Attorneys, Physicians, etc.);
(4) An encounter with a person only if the encounter is not related to an investigation.
e. Department Employees may not activate a BWC to intentionally make recordings of:
(1) Other persons in areas where a reasonable expectation of privacy exists such as locker rooms, restrooms, etc., unless necessary for investigative purposes;
(3) Any type of non-law enforcement-related personal activities;

(4) Patient care areas of medical facilities unless the recording is for official police business such as a criminal investigation, dying declaration, Horizontal Gaze Nystagmus (HGN) on injured drivers, or a specific call for police service;
(5) Juveniles unless evidentiary in nature or as authorized by the Family Code; TBP 10.02
(6) A testing area, courtroom, arbitration hearing, or disciplinary meeting with the employee’s chain of command;
(7) Classrooms when testing will be conducted unless the instructor or facilitator has authorized the device to be activated during the meeting or class;
(8) Solely for the purpose of surveillance or identification of individuals engaged in constitutionally protected activities conducted in a lawful manner.

f. An Investigating Employee who does not activate a body worn camera in response to a call for assistance must include in the Investigating Employee’s incident report or otherwise note in the case file or record the reason for not activating the camera. Whether the reason is justified not to activate the body worn camera because it is unsafe, unrealistic, or impracticable is based on whether a reasonable person under the same or similar circumstances would have made the same decision.

g. At no time is a Department Employee expected to jeopardize their safety or the safety of another person in order to immediately activate their issued BWC into record mode. Any BWC not immediately activated into record mode due to the safety of a Department Employee or another person shall be placed into record mode as soon as possible.

a. When an incident has been recorded and an offense/incident report is generated, the report-writing employee shall note in the digital media evidence (DME) section of the report the existence of body-worn video. Because RMS only allows for the entry of five (5) employees in the DME section of the report, the report-writing employee shall note the first five (5) responding officers with BWCs in that section. If the incident or a portion the incident was also captured by a BWCs of additional Investigating Employees in excess of the five (5) listed in the DME section of the report, the report-writing employee shall note in the first sentence of the report narrative the existence of body-worn videos of the additional Department Employees. If the employee recording the DME is not the reporting employee, the employee recording the DME shall immediately notify the report writing employee of the existence of a DME, and if necessary supplement the report to note this.

b. If the citizen contact resulted in the issuance of a Class C misdemeanor citation, the Investigating Employee shall note on the back of the citation that DME was captured and placed on Evidence.com.

c. The employee shall label the recording with any applicable report number in the ID field. In addition, the employee shall categorize the recording as “Evidence” when appropriate. The Evidence category will be used for any recording related to Criminal (criminal offense related) or Administrative (use of force, pursuits, Investigating Employee involved traffic accidents, etc.) incidents. These tasks can be accomplished via a mobile device or by accessing Evidence.com directly.
NOTE: In the event of a non-happening, the employee will simply not categorize a recording.

d. By the end of each duty day, if the Investigating Employee’s BWC is storing DME, the device shall be placed in an appropriate docking station and should not be removed until the download of data is complete. TBP 12.08
All DME captured by BWCs shall be uploaded to Evidence.com for storage. TBP 12.08

a. In accordance with Tex. Occ. Code 1701.66, employees shall not delete, cause to be deleted, destroy, cause to be destroyed any recording from a BWC that documents an incident that involves the use of deadly force by a police department employee, or that is otherwise related to an administrative or criminal investigation of a police department employee until all criminal matters have been finally adjudicated and all related administrative investigations have concluded.
b. Evidence.com maintains DME that is categorized as Evidence indefinitely.
c. DME that is not categorized as Evidence will be retained for two and a half (2 ½) years and then deleted.
d. It is permissible to retain recordings for training exercises upon final adjudication of all associated criminal cases. TBP 12.08
5. Access to DME collected from BWCs

a. All stored DME is subject to release in accordance with the Texas Public Information Act, and/or Texas Occupations Code Ch. 1701. TBP 12.08 This includes Tex. Occ. Code 1701.66, which prohibits the public release of any recording from a BWC that documents an incident that involves the use of deadly force by a police department employee, or that is otherwise related to an administrative or criminal investigation of a police department employee, until all criminal matters have been finally adjudicated and all related administrative investigations have concluded. An exception to this rule exists if the Department determines that a public release serves a law enforcement purpose.
b. Employees may use media captured via the BWC to assist with the investigation and to promote accuracy in the completion of reports.

c. All DME captured during the scope of an employee’s duties is property of the Fort Worth Police Department/City of Fort Worth and subject to City, State, and police department policies regarding the viewing, release, retention and destruction of the same. Employees shall not convert DME for personal use, including uploading recordings to social media platforms, nor shall employees access, copy, edit or release recordings, or depictions from recordings, without proper authority and/or written approval.

d. Video captured from a BWC shall not be released to an unauthorized person. Any release without departmental permission is a violation of state law and may be punishable as a Class A Misdemeanor under Texas Code of Criminal Procedure, Article 2B.0110.

e. Non-sworn personnel in the police department shall not be permitted to view DME without permission from the employee’s immediate supervisor. Governmental employees who are directly involved in the investigation and/or prosecution of a criminal or administrative case related to the DME, who work in Internal Affairs, or are authorized by the City Manager are exempt from this provision.
f. Department employees are prohibited from divulging or using video footage for any commercial or other non-law enforcement purpose.

g. Third-party digital recording storage vendors that act as an agent of the Fort Worth Police Department in maintaining body camera footage, shall not be permitted to independently access, view or alter any video footage, except to delete videos as required by law or City retention policies, unless authorized by a police department employee. TBP 12.08
6. Officers right to review BWC footage before making a statement
a. Sworn officers may review media captured from a BWC before making any statements about an incident.

b. Sworn officers involved in a Critical Police Incident (CPI) may review media captured from their BWC prior to making a statement and should be permitted to review the media with a peer representative or another Department Employee who was not involved in the incident.
7. Supervisor and Internal Review of BWC footage
a. Supervisors who become aware of a possible violation of this policy during their normal course of duties, shall make every effort to determine if there was an actual violation.

b. Any failure to activate a BWC, or failure to activate a BWC prior to the start of an incident, shall trigger a supervisory review to determine if the failure to activate was a malfunction, user error, a deliberate act or omission, or justified because it was unsafe, unrealistic or impracticable to activate the body worn camera in accordance with this policy. The supervisor shall document the reason in Blue Team.
c. Supervisors shall specifically look at the audit trail for the body-worn camera to determine if it was powered off during the shift or prior to the incident.

d. Supervisors should document patterns of behavior associated with the failure to activate the body-worn camera in accordance with policy in Blue Team and refer to the disciplinary guidelines matrix when further action is necessary.

e. If a use of force, vehicle pursuit, or any other administrative inquiry-based personnel action related to a misconduct case is captured on a BWC, the DME(s) from the incident shall be uploaded to the administrative report by a supervisor to facilitate seamless administrative review.

f. Employees are encouraged and supported by the chain of command to flag the DME when the employee feels that they may face an unsubstantiated complaint or accusation as a result of a DME captured encounter.
g. Supervisors shall review at least three (3) random videos per Department Employee biannually. TBP 2.01

(1) When conducting bi-annual supervisory reviews/audits of Department Employees’ video, the supervisor is not required to watch each incident on an eight (8) or ten (10) hour shift; however, the supervisor shall review the footage in a manner intended to gain an understanding of that Department Employee’s performance and adherence to policy and laws related to racial profiling and bias-free policing.

(2) The bi-annual review/audit period will begin and end on the same schedule as the City of Fort Worth Performance Evaluation’s mid-year check-in (April) and the formal annual ePerformance (October) process.
(3) The review/audits will be sent to Internal Affairs through Blue Team after review by the Division Commander/Captain or the respective Deputy Chief if an infraction rises to that level.
(4) Additional audits of DME may be requested at any time by a deputy chief or above.

a. Police supervisors shall ensure that employees conduct daily inspections of the BWCs prior to each shift, to confirm the devices are operational and have sufficient battery life. Any problems with the BWC shall be reported to the supervisor immediately and the supervisor shall contact the Body Camera Program Coordinator via email on that date to secure a repair or replacement.
1. Department employees who work at any approved off-duty LE/SR job shall wear and use a BWC.
2. All procedures for the use of the BWC for Investigating Employees shall also apply to the use at approved LE/SR employment.
3. If DME is recorded during off-duty LE/SR employment, the Department employee shall place the device in the docking station by the end of the Department employee’s next scheduled on-duty shift.

4. In the event an Department employee working an off-duty LE/SR employment records an incident that needs to be downloaded immediately, whether administrative or criminal, the Department Employee shall contact an on-duty supervisor for approval to return to on-duty status for the purpose of downloading the video. If approved to return to on-duty status, the Department employee shall receive two (2) hours of administrative call-back compensation.

The in-car recording system is an effective law enforcement tool which can also provide a degree of safety and peace of mind for the Department Employee using the system. Supervisors and Department Employees shall be familiar with the Standard Operating Procedures for the In-Car Recording System and refer to that document for specific responsibilities, requirements and documentation.

1. Video Recall – allows for the review and use of video captured by a Fleet camera, even if the camera was not actively recording. Video Recall is a lower quality stream (400p at 15fps with no audio) that continuously overwrites itself after 18 hours of recording.
2. Buffering Mode (Turning on the Camera)-With the camera turned on, the Axon system is in the Buffering mode. When Buffering begins:
a. The Operation LED on the back of the camera will blink green
b. The camera will be capturing video but no audio, and will not record to permanent memory while in Buffering mode
c. Buffered video duration is 30 seconds by default
3. Event Mode – the act of causing the in-car recording system to start recording audio and video footage. The system will automatically capture one (30) second of pre-event video with no audio.
4. Tagging an Event – the act of naming or designating specific footage in Evidence.com.
5. Isolate an Event – to cause an event to be separated out from other events on the in-car camera and saved in Evidence.com.

1. Recordings generated on department-owned equipment are the property of the City of Fort Worth Police Department and shall be treated as evidence. Unless specifically authorized by this order or done in accordance with the City Document Retention Schedule, tampering with evidence (including alteration, overwriting, erasure or other efforts to purposely destroy or modify any recordings) may constitute a criminal offense and/or an administrative violation.
2. Concealing or making a vehicle inaccessible to others or taking a vehicle out of service for any amount of time in order to allow the continuous loop to record over footage is prohibited.
3. Use of department-owned recording equipment for any purpose other than authorized law enforcement action is prohibited.

4. Events written by the in-car recording systems are official documents subject to the Public Information Act and the City’s Records Retention Policy. Public Information requests for such Events shall be handled as directed in General Order 212.05, Information from Police Files, the Public Information Act and the City’s Records Retention policy.
5. Events written by the in-car recording system in situations where a Critical Police Incident has occurred shall be maintained in accordance to our current retention policy.
6. It is permissible to retain recordings for display during training exercises upon final adjudication of all associated criminal cases.
7. Violation of any portion of this order may lead to disciplinary action.
C. Maintenance of the in-car recording system
1. Prior to using the recording system, Department Employees shall receive training on the proper operation and care.

2. With the exception of positioning the camera to ensure recording from the best vantage point, Department Employees shall not remove, disconnect/unplug, power off, add other equipment, alter, relocate or otherwise change the recording equipment installed in a department vehicle. Department Employees may be subject to discipline for intentional or negligent loss of or damage to recording system equipment.

3. Department Employees will not remove, nor cause to be removed by Fleet service personnel, the in-car camera for replacement without ensuring that all stored events have been uploaded from the device to the evidence.com.

4. Third-party digital recording storage vendors that to act as an agent of the Fort Worth Police Department in maintaining body camera footage, shall not be permitted to independently access, view or alter any video footage, except to delete videos as required by law or agency retention policies.

5. Department Employees will treat the in-car recording system as equipment to be inspected as directed in General Order 507.01, Checking Out Marked Units, and will notify a supervisor of any malfunctions.
D. Operation of the in-car recording system
1. Department Employees shall log-in to the in-car video system at the beginning of every shift to insure that all videos created during their shift are assigned to them.
2. Department Employees shall cause the in-car recording system to write an event in the following situations:
a. When addressing criminal violations, investigations, and engaging in enforcement activities, including but not limited to:
(4) Pursuits - whether or not the vehicle is the primary vehicle
c. Transportation of any non-police department personnel - exceptions include Explorers, CAPA members, MAC members, and a previously approved ride-along.
d. Department Employee-involved accidents - a copy of the Event shall be made and submitted to the Accident Review Board.
e. Code 3 Operation - Department Employees will not stop the recording while the light bar is in operation and the vehicle is still moving.
f. The system may be used to record other law enforcement actions at the discretion of the Department Employee.
3. Department Employees at the scene of an extended event may stop writing an event during periods of limited citizen interaction or when no enforcement action is occurring.
4. Department Employees may temporarily deactivate the audio portion of the in-car recording system under the following circumstances, but only when no citizen contact is taking place:
a. To exchange NCIC/TCIC, DPS or other law enforcement sensitive data either in person or via the police radio or MDC,
b. To facilitate the discussion of training issues or to discuss operation strategies; and
c. To share information such as telephone numbers or personal information with another Department Employee.
5. The termination of an audio or video event with the in-car recording system will require the Department Employee to tag the event. TBP 12.08

6. If conducting a custodial interrogation near a department vehicle that is equipped with an in-car recording system, it is highly recommended that an event be written that includes recording of the Miranda warning.
7. Department Employees shall also document information about the existence of in-car camera footage in the narrative portion of their reports.

8. Events stored in Evidence.com are official documents subject to the Public Information Act and the City's Records Retention Policy. No event shall be erased or destroyed without the written approval of the relevant Deputy Chief and the Records and Information Management Office. TBP 12.08
9. All stored DME is subject to release in accordance with the Texas Public Information Act, and/or Texas Occupations Code 1701. TBP 12.08

10. Department Employees utilizing an on-Department Employee recording device in accordance with General Order 506.03, Body Worn Cameras, may elect not to wear the audio body microphone portion of the in-car video system.
